## Motivation

Part of the Q4 kernel/quantization optimization roadmap (#42473) and GLM-5.3 on SM120 tracking (#51550).

The intermediate BF16 query and per-head quantization scales need not be written back to memory.

items.author: INBreezefall
items.summary: DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash W4A8 stores each C1/C2 index key row in 256 bytes on the Ascend 910B BF16 path. This opt-in format takes 226 bytes including metadata.
items.body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1 Flash W4A8 stores each C1/C2 index key row in 256 bytes on the Ascend 910B BF16 path. This opt-in format takes 226 bytes including metadata. The measured memory saving is 11.72% per affected row. The eager implementation trades serving throughput for persistent cache capacity.

## Modifications

- Persist each 128-component C1/C2 index key as 128 signed bytes and 98 bytes of scales and selectors. Keep compressed attention KV in BF16. Reconstruct active keys for accuracy-sensitive reranking.
- Use the upstream candidate operator with signed Q/K for coarse selection

When HiCache backs up a request whose KV is larger than the entire host pool, `_execute_kv_backup` still called `evict_host(needed)` first. ## Motivation

A hung kernel or collective blocks the workers without a log line. `/health` reports a worker process that has exited, a dead broker or a dead routing loop, but not a hang (the docs say so: "The monitor does not detect arbitrary hangs"). `--scheduler-rpc-timeout` is a different bound: it fails one caller's wait, queue time included, and leaves `/health` unchanged.

items.title: [Bug] HiCache backup of oversized request evicts all host-cached prefixes before giving up
items.author: guesswhoami-ship-it
items.summary: When HiCache is enabled with a host pool smaller than the device pool, evicts all host-only evictable prefixes when a backup request exceeds the entire host pool. The eviction cannot make room because the pool is too small for the backup, so the function retur…
items.body:
## Summary

When HiCache is enabled with a host pool smaller than the device pool (`--hicache-ratio 0.5`), `_execute_kv_backup` evicts all host-only evictable prefixes when a backup request exceeds the entire host pool. The eviction cannot make room because the pool is too small for the backup, so the function returns None after the damage is done. Other requests whose prefixes were evicted lose their L2 cache hits and must recompute.

**What:** `_execute_kv_backup` calls `evict_host(needed)` without checking whether `needed` can ever fit the host pool capacity.
**Where:** `unified_radix_cache
discussion: I'd like to take this. `_execute_kv_backup` should return before `evict_host` when the backup is larger than the host pool, since eviction cannot make room. I'll open a PR with a CPU unit test shortly.

## Motivation

`GCFreezer` (#50883) freezes the scheduler heap only after the scheduler has been idle for `--gc-freeze-on-idle-secs`, and that freeze starts with a full collection. A PD prefill scheduler under sustained load is never idle, so its heap is never frozen. Every generation-2 collection then walks the whole long-lived heap and stalls the scheduler loop. Under pipeline parallelism, one stage's stall holds up the whole pipeline.

items.body:
## Motivation

On Hopper, Inkling 2 Small runs TP8/EP8 with no MoE a2a backend: every rank sees all tokens, runs the 48 of the 384 routed experts it owns (a contiguous id range), and each MoE layer ends in an all-reduce. With contiguous ranges the expert load is uneven: in routing recorded on 8x H200 with the cookbook recipe, the busiest rank gets about 1.5x the mean rows, at c64 decode and in 8K prefill chunks alike, and every layer waits for it.

EPLB's static placement already covers this for other MoE models: `--init-expert-location <counts or map>` reassigns experts to ranks at load time.

items.title: [Bugfix][Attention] TRTLLM prefill with BF16 query and FP8 KV applies k/v scales once
items.author: hao-aaron
items.summary: Fixes double-application of k/v quantization scales in TRTLLM FP8 KV cache prefill path, where BF16 query path incorrectly multiplied scales twice causing incorrect output.
items.body:
## Purpose

TRTLLM prefill with a BF16 query and an FP8 KV cache applied the k/v scales twice. This path first dequantizes the pages it reads with `trtllm_prefill_attn_kvfp8_dequant`, which already multiplies K by `k_scale` and V by `v_scale`; the kernel then also got `bmm1_scale = scale · q_scale · k_scale` and `bmm2_scale = v_scale`. Prefill and decode disagreed whenever the scales were not 1.0 (cold-start bug). The kernel now gets `bmm1_scale = scale` and `bmm2_scale = 1.0` on this path; a BF16 query has no `q_scale` and no fused output quant (that requires an FP8 query). Part of RFC #54477

## Purpose

`XPUPlatform.get_attn_backend_cls` raises "Invalid attention backend for xpu" when `FLEX_ATTENTION` is requested explicitly, although the FlexAttention backend runs on XPU: `torch` flex attention compiles through Triton XPU, and the backend's only CUDA-specific code is guarded by `torch.cuda.is_available()`. items.title: [Perf] rust-server: Decode each chunk's own bytes for byte-level BPE tokenizers
items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: The Rust server's detokenizer shards decode every stream through dynamo-tokenizers', which on each step re-decodes all ids since its last complete text and moves its offsets only when the text grew and does not end in U+FFFD. A stream whose text never complete…
items.body:
## Motivation

The Rust server's detokenizer shards decode every stream through dynamo-tokenizers' `DecodeStream`, which on each step re-decodes all ids since its last complete text and moves its offsets only when the text grew and does not end in U+FFFD. A stream whose text never completes, such as a run of skipped special tokens or stray bytes that keep the text ending in U+FFFD, never moves them: each token costs O(output length) and the request O(n²). That work runs on the shard thread that serves every request hashed to it, and with more shards the single from-scheduler dispatcher blocks

## Motivation

Every JIT module builds for the local GPU's arch-specific target (`sm_100a` on CC 10.0, `sm_103a` on CC 10.3), so a build cache shared across the devices of one family holds one build per device, and a warm-up compiles each module once per device. Most modules use nothing that only the arch-specific target has, and one family build (`sm_100f`) would serve them all. Which modules can take the family build is a per-module question, so the choice belongs to the module.

The Triton MoE path computes SiTU between the two expert GEMMs with separate FP32 PyTorch ops, even though SGLang already has a fused CUDA SiTU kernel, `situ_and_mul`.

items.title: Activation checkpointing runs during torch.no_grad()
items.author: sbhavani
items.summary: tensor_parallel.checkpoint incorrectly enters checkpointed forward mode under torch.no_grad, queuing states for a backward recompute that never executes during RL log-prob computation.
items.body:
**Describe the bug**

`tensor_parallel.checkpoint()` enters `CheckpointFunction` under `torch.no_grad()`. The wrapped forward sees `is_checkpointing() == True` and can queue state for a backward recompute that never runs. 

Miles hit this during forward-only RL log-probability computation. [code](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/f0987cfeb8d358637cddd054e270f757a0dd53cf/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/random.py#L796)

**Steps/Code to reproduce bug**

With a CUDA tensor `x`, run `checkpoint(fn, False, x)` inside `torch.no_grad()`. Have `fn` print `is_checkpointing()`. It prints `True`.

items.title: [Fix] speculative: Exact sampling penalties and min_new_tokens in DFlash and DSpark verify
items.author: metamergebot
items.summary: Fixes DFlash/DSpark speculative verification ignoring penalty fields (frequency/presence/repetition_penalty, min_new_tokens) by counting each committed draft token in verify-row penalty tables.
items.body:
## Motivation

DFlash and DSpark verify ignore `frequency_penalty`, `presence_penalty`, `repetition_penalty` and `min_new_tokens`. Nothing counts the tokens they commit in the penalty tables, and verify reads `acc_linear_penalties`, a field that `SamplingBatchInfo` does not have. So a request with `min_new_tokens` can stop early, and a request with a repetition penalty gets the same logits as one without.

This PR counts every committed token and penalizes each verify row as decoding one token at a time would. The results are bitwise equal to non-speculative decoding.

items.title: [Perf][Core] Pack the consumed audio of streaming sessions
items.author: andylolu2
items.summary: Stacked on #68539: only the last commit, 6201477, is new here. A streaming input session keeps the feature of every audio chunk, so that it can replay them after a preemption.
items.body:
## Overview

Stacked on #68539: only the last commit, 6201477, is new here.

A streaming input session keeps the feature of every audio chunk, so that it can replay them after a preemption. Each kept feature is about 15 objects that the cyclic GC tracks, across the scheduler and the workers. A full collection therefore gets slower the longer a session runs. This PR packs the features of the chunks that have been consumed into arrays and a few byte buffers, so each one leaves no tracked objects behind.

This is a proof of concept, opened as a draft. It has no end-to-end serving benchmark yet.

## Summary

With optimistic prefill, a PD prefill worker can finish a request before its decode worker has reserved memory for it; the finished KV then stays with the request ("parked") until the decode reservation arrives. A request that already holds its decode reservation (bootstrapped) can be refused prefill KV because parked requests hold the pool, while those parked requests wait for the decode memory the bootstrapped request already holds. Neither side moves until a PD timeout fails one of them. This change lets one parked request give its KV back in that case.

## Overview

FlashInfer benchmarks several kernel tactics for an operation and input shape, then saves the winner in a per-rank table. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash’s TP4 low-latency decode starts that search inside `load_model`. On a warm restart all four tables can already be on disk. shared entry point. Adding PPU would mean a third copy, or having PPU import
someone else's module, and neither belongs in main.

items.title: [Bugfix][Distributed] Gate MNNVL buffer setup on multicast support
items.author: HansG89
items.summary: Gates MNNVL symmetric-memory buffer initialization on multicast capability, preventing useless allocations and collective rendezvous crashes on non-multicast GPUs like L20.
items.body:
Fixes #68916.

## Problem

CustomAllreduce construction calls torch symmetric memory empty() and rendezvous() on every CUDA device during group init, without the capability gate that SymmMemCommunicator already applies to the same API (the "Device capability 8.9 not supported" line in the issue is that gate). On GPUs without multicast, e.g. L20, the call can never produce a usable buffer: rendezvous returns multicast_ptr == 0 and the result is discarded. The rendezvous is a collective over the group store and has a known host-level crash on 2-rank gloo groups (pytorch/pytorch#203740). Since #5

items.title: [CI][ROCm] Layer math in the float64 reference (T2 of #68016)
items.author: divakar-amd
items.summary: Adds a shared float64 reference implementation for layer math operations (normalize, rotate, attend, route) in specialized decode kernels to provide a consistent numerical yardstick across all ROCm models.
items.body:
## TL;DR

A "specialized decode" kernel is one hand-written GPU kernel that does the work of a whole
transformer layer in a single launch. To know whether it is *right*, a test needs something to
compare against. Today each model brings its own answer key, so two models can disagree about what a
normalization or a softmax even is, and both tests pass.

This PR writes the answer key once, in float64, and shares it: the four pieces of layer math every
specialized decode does — normalize, rotate, attend, route. 79 new tests, CPU-only, 26 s.

```

## Motivation

`--speculative-token-map` crashes at startup when the target `lm_head` is quantized.

items.title: [Feat] dspark-dflash: Sample greedy drafts at temperature 1000 by default under simulated acceptance
items.author: jasperjiaguo
items.summary: Changes DSpark and DFLASH drafters to sample greedy drafts at temperature 1000 under forced acceptance, preventing output from collapsing into short repeating token loops that skew benchmark results.
items.body:
## Motivation

Forced acceptance (`SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`) is the usual way to measure DSpark and DFLASH decode cost at a fixed acceptance length. It commits whatever the drafter proposes, so with greedy requests the committed tokens are far from real generation:

- **DSpark:** the greedy drafter's output collapses into short repeating loops early in the output.
- **DFLASH:** the default `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=fixed` commits token id `100` at every accepted position. `real-draft-token` commits the greedy drafts instead, and they loop the same way.

# tl;dr

This PR adds support for Kitty KV-cache quantization to vLLM through `--kv-cache-dtype kitty` and a dedicated attention backend. Kitty reduces KV-cache memory usage by quantizing values and most key channels to 2 bits, while dynamically boosting selected key channels to 4 bits. It retains attention sink tokens and recent tokens in the model's original precision to help preserve accuracy during long-context generation.

The implementation is based on the [original Kitty paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.18643) and the authors' [GitHub repository](https://github.com/Summer-Summer/Kitty)

items.title: [Fix] pd: Wait for the forward before transferring intermediate PP prefill chunks
items.author: garry569
items.summary: With PP in PD disaggregation, the schedule stream may only wait for the launched forward's shared reads (the read-done fast path, e.g. extend), not for its KV writes.
items.body:
## Motivation

With PP in PD disaggregation, the schedule stream may only wait for the launched forward's shared reads (the read-done fast path, e.g. `trtllm_mha` extend), not for its KV writes. Without overlap, the PP prefill loop sends the previous chunk of a chunked request from `process_prefill_chunk` while the forward that computes that chunk can still be running, so the KV transfer can read KV that is not written yet. The early cached-prefix send has the same gap under PP, since it only records a forward event under overlap.

Affected: PD prefill with `--pp-size > 1`, multi-chunk request

items.title: [Bugfix][Model] Replicate encoder layers at non-divisible TP sizes
items.author: majq92
items.summary: Several multimodal encoders shard their attention by head count and their MLP by intermediate size. When the tensor-parallel size does not divide those dimensions, the sharding layers raise while the model is being constructed, so the model cannot be loaded at…
items.body:
## Overview

Several multimodal encoders shard their attention by head count and their MLP by
intermediate size. When the tensor-parallel size does not divide those
dimensions, the sharding layers raise while the model is being constructed, so
the model cannot be loaded at all:

```
AssertionError: 20 is not divisible by 8
```

`ensure_divisibility` (`vllm/distributed/utils.py`) asserts, and
`QKVParallelLinear.__init__` calls it before any weight is allocated.

| Model | Encoder | heads | TP sizes that fail |

The NVLS AllGather-V and ReduceScatter-V kernels, and the ordered ReduceScatter-V used by batch-invariant mode, returned before their barrier when a CTA's `pid >= ep_max_tokens`. ## Overview

On MI355X, MoRIIO PD serving can fail at the first requests with `HIP error 209` while VRAM is free: amdgpu counts `hipMalloc` VRAM that a NIC pins twice in the KFD allocation limit ([ROCm/mori#721](https://github.com/ROCm/mori/issues/721)). items.title: [trainer, worker] feat: keep per-micro-batch scalar metrics on device, read them back lazily in one batch
items.author: jialei777
items.summary: Removes the per-micro-batch host syncs that verl's PPO loss path forces between forward and backward. call on / /, and calls on every scalar tensor metric (,,,...).
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Removes the per-micro-batch host syncs that verl's PPO loss path forces between forward and backward.

`compute_policy_loss_*` call `.item()` on `pg_clipfrac` / `ppo_kl` / `pg_clipfrac_lower`, and `Metric.append` calls `.item()` on every scalar tensor metric (`actor/pg_loss`, `actor/old_logprobs_mismatch_count`, `kl_loss`, ...). Both run inside the loss function, before `loss.backward()`. On an asynchronous accelerator each `.item()` blocks the host until the micro-batch forward has finished on the device, so the device idles while the host then traces and dispatches

A request whose image embeddings are already available through an EC connector can still wait behind a local encoder run. Check for the external hit before testing the remaining encoder compute budget, so a chunked prefill can use the decoder tokens left in the step.

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8766.

In V1 trainers (`sync` and `colocate_async`), `_compute_advantage()` whitens advantages once over the full sampled batch, whereas `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()` splits the batch into `ppo_mini_batch_size` optimizer chunks without re-normalizing per chunk. When the sampled batch is larger than `ppo_mini_batch_size`, individual optimizer chunks can have non-zero token-weighted advantage means, introducing chunk-level policy-gradient drift.

This PR re-normalizes `mini_batch_td["advantages"]` per optimizer chunk in `TrainingWorker.train_mini_batch()`

items.title: [Bug] TransferQueue drops samples after a 30 s ACK timeout, then compute_log_prob fails with KeyError: 'loss_mask' (Qwen2-7B GSM8K GRPO recipe)
items.author: AmineDiro
items.summary: On verl v0.9.1, verl's own Qwen2-7B-Instruct GRPO GSM8K recipe (the baseline in ) crashed twice on 8x B200, both times on the first training step after a validation pass. Right before the crash, the agent-loop workers log and carry on.
items.body:
## Summary

On verl v0.9.1, verl's own Qwen2-7B-Instruct GRPO GSM8K recipe (the `qwen2-7b-fsdp2.log` baseline in `docs/algo/baseline.md`) crashed twice on 8x B200, both times on the first training step after a validation pass. Right before the crash, the agent-loop workers log `Timeout waiting for data status update ACK from controller after 30s` and carry on. The data was written to storage but the controller never marks it ready, so the trainer later gets an empty batch from TransferQueue and fails with `KeyError: 'loss_mask'` in `compute_log_prob`.

The timeout itself is a slow controller.

items.title: Retire engines that died during training before the weight update
items.author: GaokaiZhang
items.summary: An engine that dies in that window stays registered in the router and in the engine list. The next sends it, the request fails with, and the run stops.
items.body:
## Problem

The health monitors are paused from the end of a rollout (`finish_rollout`) to the weight update. An engine that dies in that window stays registered in the router and in the engine list. The next `update_weights` sends it `pause_generation`, the request fails with `ConnectionRefusedError`, and the run stops. With the fully-async rollout the periodic check does not help either: each resume restarts the first wait (600 s by default), so no periodic check runs when a rollout takes less than that. Details and the traceback: #2551.

items.author: GaokaiZhang
items.summary: pauses them and runs one check ( and → ). Nothing checks again until the next resumes them.
items.body:
### Bug Description

The health monitors are paused from the end of a rollout to the weight update. `finish_rollout` pauses them and runs one check (`slime/ray/rollout.py:332` and `:403` → `slime/ray/serving.py:280`). Nothing checks again until the next `generate` resumes them (`rollout.py:322`). An engine that dies inside that window (SGLang server crash, OOM, node fault) stays in the router and in the engine list.

# What does this PR do?

Drops two full-tensor copies on the SBHD sparse indexer-loss path in `FusedCSAIndexerSparseAttnFunc`: `query` and the compressed KV are no longer made contiguous after the `[s, b] -> [b, s]` permute before `_compute_attn_target`.

items.body:
## Description

This PR adds DeCo-Attention to VisualGen as an opt-in quantized-attention recipe of the `CUTEDSL` backend. The QK product of self-attention runs on NVFP4 operands, with the quantization error of the scores compensated inside the same matrix product; the PV product runs in FP8, or in NVFP4 on SM120. On Wan2.2 T2V at 720p the denoising is 1.68x faster than with BF16 attention on GB300, 1.73x on Rubin and 1.69x to 1.85x on RTX PRO 6000.

It is off by default and enabled per configuration:

```yaml
attention_config:
  backend: CUTEDSL
  quant_attention_config:
    qk_dtype: nvfp4
discussion:

Since the rubin kernels are the same as the blackwell ones, I think we don't need to make a separate rubin folder. This PR's organization

This PR lets git worktrees of TensorRT-LLM share one ccache. A fresh worktree then reuses the objects that another worktree already compiled, so its first build is much faster.

Before this PR, a fresh worktree missed ccache for every compile. ccache keys each object on its compile command, and that command holds the absolute paths of the source and build folders. A worktree at a new path therefore gets new keys. ccache's `base_dir` setting fixes this, but each user has to configure it. CI configures it in `jenkins/controlCCache.groovy`.

items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

**Problem.** A `kv_cache_compression_config` method with a cold-page codec (today `quantization_for_cold_page`, NVFP4) makes `KVCacheManagerV2` encode pages when they leave the GPU for its host, disk or remote tiers. The `mooncake-store` connector takes the place of those tiers (it forces `host_cache_size` / `disk_cache_size` to 0 for roles that transfer KV), but it moved raw GPU pages, so with both configured the compression setting silently had no effect on the pool.

**Solution.** The connector now stores pages through the KV cache manager's own codec

items.body:
@coderabbitai summary

## Description

The qwen4_exp cache manager keeps a QSA index-key plane next to the K/V pool. A page holds one row per token (`tokens_per_block`, 32): the token's raw index key, overwritten at the last token of each `compress_ratio` group by the group's compressed key. Index scoring reads only the compressed keys; a raw key is read once more, to pool its group, and is dead after that.

items.title: [Feature Request]Support FP32 bias gradient accumulation in native fused Linear backward
items.author: zjjott
items.summary: Extends fused gradient accumulation in native Megatron-LM Linear backward to accumulate bias gradients directly in FP32 instead of BF16, eliminating ~1.67e-3 relative L2 error.
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

When `gradient_accumulation_fusion=True`, native `LinearWithGradAccumulationAndAsyncCommunication` can accumulate weight gradients directly into FP32 `main_grad`, but its bias gradient still passes through BF16 before reaching the FP32 DDP buffer.

The relevant code is [`grad_bias = grad_output.sum(dim=0)` in layers.py](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/dev/megatron/core/tensor_parallel/layers.py#L962). With BF16 `grad_output`, this returns a BF16 result. Subsequent FP32 accumulation cannot recover the lost precision.

items.title: [algo, trainer, fsdp, megatron, cfg, doc] feat: add topk_rb KL loss (top-k Rao-Blackwellised KL to the reference)
items.author: hiddevandebeek
items.summary: It adds, a KL penalty against the reference policy for. The estimator computes KL(πθ ‖ πref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Implements the RFC in #8536. It adds `actor.kl_loss_type: topk_rb`, a KL penalty against the reference policy for `use_kl_loss=True`.

The estimator computes KL(π_θ ‖ π_ref) exactly over the reference top-k tokens plus one tail bucket. The within-tail part is estimated from the sampled token, so the result is an **unbiased** estimate of the full-vocabulary KL gradient at every k, with much lower variance than the single-sample `kl`/`k2`/`low_var_kl`/`k3+` options. It is the per-token Rao-Blackwellised KL of [Amini et al., NeurIPS 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.1063

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Preserve vLLM's `finish_reason="length"` in `TokenOutput.stop_reason`. Today the vLLM rollout server reports `completed` both when generation stops naturally and when the output budget cuts it off. A caller translating this value to the Anthropic Messages API consequently sends `end_turn` for a truncated response, and the client can exit with work still in progress.

### Design and compatibility

Map vLLM's `stop` to `completed` and let `length` pass through the existing fallback. Callers can now return `max_tokens` to Anthropic clients. Abort still maps to `aborted`

### What does this PR do?

Restore bounded layered LoRA collection for FSDP1 layouts with flattened parameters or independently wrapped adapter leaves. The collector currently checks local parameter names, passes local keys to PEFT, and recursively summons nested units. These behaviors can drop adapters or export a nested `_flat_param`. Initialize FSDP1 from its real root, recognize original flat-parameter names and leaf prefixes, normalize parameter ownership

items.title: [reward] fix: compare prime_code call-based outputs as plain builtins
items.author: Aarav500
items.summary: In, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of or whose always returns got full reward on every call-based task.
items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Fixes #8656. In `prime_code`, call-based tests compared the generated function's return value with `output == expected`. The generated code controls that object, so a subclass of `int` or `list` whose `__eq__` always returns `True` got full reward on every call-based task. Swapping the operands doesn't help, because Python tries a subclass's reflected `__eq__` first.

This adds `_to_builtin()` in `prime_code/testing_util.py` and applies it to the output right after the existing `json.dumps(output)` call. It rebuilds the value from plain `None`/`bool`/`int`/`float

Checkpoint participants each own one GPU, but Ray's default first barrier can enroll every visible GPU and its rendezvous key contains the local ordinal. `Float16Module.forward` upcasts the last pipeline stage's output to fp32 by default. slime calls the actor with `labels=None`, so the whole `[T, V]` logits tensor is copied to fp32. It is the largest single allocation in a long-context actor step: 40,960 tokens × 248,320 vocabulary is about 41 GB in fp32 versus 20 GB in bf16.

items.title: fix(data): give uniform reward groups exactly zero advantage
items.author: saloni-garg
items.summary: When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about …
items.body:
## What does this PR do?

When every rollout in a prompt group gets the same fractional reward, there is no preference between them, so every advantage in the group should be exactly zero. In `_post_process_rewards` the group is centered in float32, and for identical rewards that can leave a residue of about an ulp instead of zero. With std normalization on, the residue is then divided by its own std, which turns it into a small nonzero advantage shared by the whole group.

Small reproduction on current main (a group of 16 rollouts that all scored 0.3, `grpo` with `grpo_std_normalization`):

-
discussion: The nonzero advantages for uniform fractional rewards reproduce on `main`. I ran the grouped-reward tests at `0063710` on CPU with PyTorch 2.13.0: uniform groups produce exact zeros, and the mixed-group and nonfinite-reward cases pass too.
Thank you for checking, and for reproducing it on main as well. Glad the tests hold up on your side too. Happy to run anything else you would like to see here.

`grade_answer_verl` (`slime/rollout/rm_hub/math_utils.py:485`) starts with:

Labels are passed through from the dataset as-is (`slime/utils/data.py:272`), so a zero answer arrives as `0` or `0.0`. ## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.title: fix(agent): terminate timed-out sandbox process groups
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: There was also a race between launch acknowledgement and publishing the detached process group PID. It does not alter the sandbox provider interface or command output contract.
items.body:
## Background

`exec_and_wait` launches commands in detached sessions so they can survive transport retries, but its timeout and cancellation paths previously stopped waiting without stopping the detached command.

## Problem

A timed-out or cancelled sandbox command could keep running and mutate the sandbox after the caller had already moved on. There was also a race between launch acknowledgement and publishing the detached process group PID.

## Solution

## Problem

`MegatronTrainRayActor.init()` backs up the actor and then loads reference, teacher, or old-actor checkpoints into the same model.

Without `--offload-train`, initialization leaves the last auxiliary checkpoint active. Both training entry points synchronize rollout weights before the first training step, so distributed or disk-based synchronization can publish auxiliary weights instead of the resumed actor.

For one resumed run:

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

Fixes #200.

Aborted samples keep `reward=None`. On the default GRPO path that list was passed to `torch.tensor`, which crashes. Custom generate functions that abort (e.g. Search-R1 tool failure) hit this.

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

## Fix

items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

I was poking at `--multimodal-keys` with a dataset that mixes image rows and plain
text rows, and ended up finding three separate problems in `_build_messages`.

### The prompt gets shattered when a row has no media

The placeholder split builds a regex alternation out of whatever media the row
